editorial.headline: Radiation Equipment Leasing: Open Nationally, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This operational-leasing activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks registration at a Bali address.
editorial.body:
At its core, this is the commercial provision of machinery and radiation equipment on rent or by operational lease, where the arrangement gives the user access without an option to buy. The stated sphere is broad enough to include equipment deployed in industrial processes, construction and other applications. A useful concrete example in the record is baggage-scanning equipment that uses an ionising-radiation source. The category therefore describes a way of supplying specialised equipment for work: the provider rents or operationally leases the machine or radiation equipment, while ownership does not pass through an option to purchase. That distinction is the backbone of the activity’s stated scope.

Who can register it? The scope is open to businesses at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That is a wide stated range, but it does not alter what the activity is: the same rental or no-option operational-leasing work, focused on machinery and radiation equipment used in the described settings. The scale list is significant because it places the activity in reach of enterprises from Mikro through Besar, rather than assigning it to one size of operator. For a founder reading the classification, the clean takeaway is to keep the commercial description aligned with the recorded activity—providing access to this equipment through rental or operational leasing without a purchase option.

Nationally, the position is open. The record marks foreign investment as TERBUKA and permits foreign ownership up to 100%, citing Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In the national framework recorded here, a PMA business can therefore participate in this activity with full foreign ownership. It is important to read that statement for exactly what it says: 100% is the national foreign-ownership ceiling, and the national status is open. This is a clear national position for the leasing activity described in the record.

Bali produces a different outcome. The Bali status is a moratorium closure, and the record is direct: a foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA at a Bali address today. The stated reason is that the Besar scale is classified as Low risk, bringing it within Bali’s island-wide, permanent PMA block for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. National openness therefore does not produce a Bali PMA registration route for this activity. This is not a Bali-specific reduction of the foreign-ownership ceiling. Bali blocks the registration itself under its PMA moratorium, notwithstanding the national permission for up to 100% foreign ownership.
